AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To evaluate the prevalence of clavicle fractures in professional and amateur cyclists and evaluate the factors associated with its occurrence.

AbstractText.Label: METHOD
AbstractText.content: One hundred and forty professional and amateur athletes were interviewed through a questionnaire regarding age and time practicing bicycling, among others.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Among the 140 evaluated cyclists, there were 19 (13.5%) clavicle fractures associated with this sports modality.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: There was a positive association between time practicing bicycling and frequency of clavicle fractures, as well as between hours of weekly training and clavicle fractures. Level of Evidence IV, Case-Series.
